subject: Snowflake vs BigQuery + Metabase — cost modeling & demo scheduling
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Snowflake vs BigQuery + Metabase — cost modeling & vendor kickoff

Team —

We're at the point where we need a short, defensible recommendation for our analytics platform refresh. Primary options on the table: (1) Snowflake core + Metabase for BI and (2) BigQuery + Metabase (we're also considering Looker but want to avoid an extra license move for now).

Please help with two things this week:
- Monica: build a vendor-agnostic TCO model (12- and 24-month) that includes storage, compute, concurrency, SSO/KMS costs, egress, and support add-ons. Put assumptions per line.
- Marcus/Rachel: provide a rough signal on query/latency patterns we should model (peak concurrency in queries/minute, typical avg slot usage, retention windows).
- Michael: any infra constraints (VPC peering, private connectivity) that would materially change vendor pricing?

I'd like to run vendor pricing calls the week of 11/8 and vendor technical demos the week after. Please cc any vendor contacts you want invited; I'm happy to coordinate calendar invites.

Thanks — getting this right matters for 2027 unit economics.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Data Platform | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Laura —

Attached is a short procurement checklist I've started (procurement_checklist.pdf). High-level constraints and asks I need from the team to finish the TCO: 

- Budget guardrail: prefer to keep steady-state unit cost delta under +20% vs current (we'll quantify after model).
- Contracting: we should assume 12-month and 24-month commitments; list any early termination or true-up clauses.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 + KMS + audit logs retention 365 days.
- Data residency: US only for now.
- SLA & credits: draft minimum latency and availability thresholds we care about.

Timeline: please get me Marcus' query patterns and Michael's network constraints by 11/4. I'll compile a first-pass model (sheet linked in drive) and share with vendors ahead of pricing calls.

Attachments: procurement_checklist.pdf (1 page checklist)

—Monica
Monica Patel

Subject: Snowflake pricing proposal & quick follow-up

Hi Laura / team —

Thanks for the heads-up. Attaching a concise proposal that maps to the checklist Monica shared (Snowflake_Proposal_ACME_v2.xlsx). Quick highlights:
- We recommend a mix of on-demand compute for spiky workloads + 24-month capacity reservation for steady ETL pipelines to optimize cost.
- Storage (AWS S3) pricing is straightforward; we included an estimated micro-billing for active/long-term storage tiers.
- Concurrency scaling will materially impact price — we modeled two concurrency scenarios (50 qps vs 200 qps).

If helpful, I can set up two sessions: an engineering demo with our sales engineer and a commercial call to walk the guarantee/discount mechanics.

Attachments: Snowflake_Proposal_ACME_v2.xlsx (pricing workbook)

Best,

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@google.com>

Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: BigQuery pricing and CUD options for Redwood

Hi Laura / team —

Appreciate the invite. I've attached our BigQuery pricing brief (BQ_CUD_pricing_2026.pdf) and included a short note on Committed Use Discounts (CUD) for slots — for many analytics-heavy customers a 1–3 year CUD materially reduces per-query costs.

Two quick items to call out:
1) Ingest & Storage: BigQuery separates storage vs compute; if you have heavy long-term archival, storage will dominate.
2) Slot sizing: for Metabase / ad-hoc dashboards, steady slot capacity helps with concurrency; we can size to your reported peak concurrency.

We can coordinate a joint demo with Metabase Consulting (cc'd) so they can speak to connection patterns and recommended infra for dashboards.

Attachments: BQ_CUD_pricing_2026.pdf (4 pages)

Regards,
Priya Shah
Cloud Solutions Architect | Google Cloud

Subject: Re: Snowflake vs BigQuery + Metabase — cost modeling & demo scheduling

Thanks all — good traction. Quick summary and proposed next steps (feel free to edit):

Summary:
- Monica will finalize the 12/24-month TCO (assumptions in the drive link) by EOD 11/7.
- Snowflake provided a pricing workbook; they will include a second tab showing caching vs non-caching scenarios.
- Google provided CUD options and suggested a joint Metabase integration session.

Evaluation rubric (we'll use this to compare apples-to-apples):
- 24-month TCO (storage + compute + egress + support)
- Query latency at 95th percentile for our two typical workloads
- Operational overhead (admin time, backups, patching, connectivity)
- Observability & traceability (token-level cost breakdown + query provenance)
- Contract flexibility (true-up, termination, data export)

Action items / schedule:
- Monica: final TCO + assumptions — due 11/7 (drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-cost-model-v1)
- Laura: schedule vendor pricing calls week of 11/8 (30–45m each).
- Marcus/Rachel: provide representative query samples for the vendor tech demos by 11/8.
- Monica/Laura: invite procurement and legal to the commercial call if numbers look close.

Proposed demo cadence (please reply with conflicts):
- 11/10 10:00am PST — Snowflake engineering demo (30m) + 30m pricing follow-up with Alex
- 11/11 11:00am PST — BigQuery + Metabase joint demo (45m)

If that aligns, Monica and I will send calendar invites and include a short NDA + SOW template for Metabase (Metabase_SOW_draft.docx attached for review).

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
